Commentary.Commentary: The third session of Day 4 is about to begin! The umpires and players enter the field. Abdullah Shafique and Imam-ul-Haq are the openers for Pakistan. Tim Southee starts with the new ball. Here we go...
... THIRD INNINGS ...

Tea has been taken now on Day 4! Pakistan have their task cut out on this tricky surface. They have their backs to the wall and need their batters to adopt a more sensible approach in the second innings. Do join us in a short while for their reply...

It was hard work on the field for the home team. Wickets didn't come their way easily. Still, credit to Abrar Ahmed for picking a 5-for. Nauman Ali though was the standout bowler. He picked only three wickets but plenty of opportunities went down off his bowling.

Earlier, powered by a big century stand for the opening wicket, New Zealand set the tone brilliantly in reply to Pakistan's 438 and Tom Latham's hundred put them in control. Pakistan tried to make a comeback but hardly succeeded in picking wickets at regular intervals. Kane Williamson was the fulcrum of the Kiwi batting as he stitched in handy partnerships throughout his stay in the middle. He went on to complete his fifth double century in Tests - the most by a New Zealander - and that was the moment Tim Southee decided to declare with a lead of 174 runs.

It's been a commanding batting show by the touring team! They batted in the afternoon session with control and the wickets started to fall only when they decided to go for quick runs. The century stand between Kane Williamson and Ish Sodhi has to be the highlight of the New Zealand innings as that helped them in gaining this handy lead.

FIFTH DOUBLE CENTURY IN TESTS FOR WILLIAMSON, the most by a Kiwi batter! It's been a resolute knock from the former skipper. Unmatched brilliance. A spectacle that everyone has enjoyed. He reaches there by nudging a full ball through square leg for a single. The New Zealand dressing room is on its feet and Tim Southee has decided to declare on 612/9.
FOUR! Slower through the air and fuller on off, Kane Williamson moves forward and lofts it over extra cover for a boundary. He moves to 199 now!
Bowls it on off, Kane Williamson eases it to mid off again.
Another fuller one, on middle, Kane Williamson blocks it to mid off again.
Just one wicket left to fall, so the afternoon session has been extended by 30 minutes.
Fuller and on off, Kane Williamson defends it to mid off.
Slower through the air, full and around off, Patel lunges to defend again but gets an inside edge onto the pads.
Tosses it outside off, Patel defends off the front foot towards gully.
Fuller and on middle, Ajaz Patel blocks it to short leg.
Bowls it outside off, turning in, Ajaz Patel looks to defend it but gets a hit on his pads. A loud appeal for lbw but the umpire is unmoved. Impact is outside off, clearly.
Another one on off, Ajaz Patel defends it to the vacant silly point region again.
Tossed up, on off, angling in, Ajaz Patel lunges to defend but it beats his bat and strikes him on the pads. Outside the line of the stumps though.
Flatter and on leg, Kane Williamson moves forward and drives it straight back at the bowler this time. Pakistan have an entire over to bowl at Ajaz Patel now.
Tosses it up, on middle. Kane Williamson blocks it back towards the bowler.
Fuller and on off, Kane Williamson defends it to mid on.
Slightly shorter one, Kane Williamson hangs back and punches it down to short extra covers.
This one lands on middle and leg, Kane Williamson defends it to mid on.
Bowls it on middle, Kane Williamson eases it to the man at point.
Bowls it outside leg, Kane Williamson reverse-sweeps it to point for one. He keeps strike for the next over.
Bowls it outside leg, Kane Williamson paddles it but finds the man at short fine leg.
Pitching outside leg, Kane Williamson looks to paddle it but misses.
Another one outside leg, Kane Williamson pads it away.
Bowls it down leg, Kane Williamson moves forward to defend it with pads but leaves it alone in the end.
This one lands outside leg, Kane pads it away.

SHOUT FOR AN LBW! This one lands just outside off, Ajaz Patel moves forward to defend it but gets beaten and gets a rap on his back pad. A loud appeal but the umpire is unmoved. Pakistan are out of reviews! The replays show that the impact is with the umpire's call and it's the same for hitting the wickets.
This one lands outside off, Kane Williamson hangs back and guides it towards covers for one. Ajaz Patel has one ball to survive again.
Slightly shorter and on middle, Kane Williamson moves forward and tucks it to mid-wicket.
This one lands down leg, Kane Williamson looks to sweep it but misses.

SIX! All the way. Tosses it on the middle stump line, Kane Williamson dances down the track and lofts it over long on for a maximum. Kane Williamson moves to 193 now! This is the third time he has ventured into this territory against Pakistan in Tests. He has a double century against them and also got out on 192 once, in Sharjah.
Fuller and on off, turning away, Kane Williamson looks to block it but gets an inside edge onto the pads.

Huge shout for a bat-pad but the umpire remains unmoved. No reviews left for Pakistan. Floated one, full and around off, Patel tries to defend but it spins back in to beat his bat. It pops out off his pads and the short leg fielder catches the ball. They appeal but to no avail. The replays find no inside edge. It was Patel's bat brushing the inside part of his pad.
Flatter delivery, close to leg, Williamson moves back and works it to deep square leg for a run. Ajaz has one ball to survive.
Down the leg side, again the batter pads it away.
Another one down the leg side and Williamson feels it's not worthy to touch his bat. Pads it away.
Action replay of the previous delivery. Williamson is not taking any chances so far.
Flighted and down the leg side, Kane pads it away.
Wide! This one is down the leg side, Williamson leaves.
Ajaz Patel is the last batter.

OUT! TAKEN! Abrar has yet another 5-wicket haul in Tests, it has been a long hard toil but it has paid dividends. Flighted and full, around off, Wagner again attempts to play the reverse sweep but this time it catches his gloves and loops behind the keeper. Agha Salman takes a simple catch moving across from slip. This is the third wicket gone done in this manner in this inning. New Zealand lead by 159 runs.
Commentary.Howout: c Agha Salman b Abrar Ahmed

Commentary.Commentary: That is defended solidly off the front foot.
Shout for an lbw, not given. Flighted around middle, spinning down, Neil Wagner tries to play the reverse sweep but misses. Going down, perhaps! Pakistan have no reviews left.
Fuller and on off, at 84 kph, Wagner defends it to short leg.
This one is generously tossed up by Abrar, full and dipping in around off, Wagner pushes it defensively to covers.
Fullish and angling down the leg side, Kane sweeps it to fine leg and picks up a single.
A touch fuller this time, around off, Wagner again defends it from the back foot.
Turning into the batter from outside off, again the length is short and Wagner defends it from the back foot.
Flatter and on off, short in length, Wagner goes on the back foot and defends it to short mid-wicket.
Neil Wagner is the next batter.

OUT! Southee holes out! Pakistan have two wickets in no time, something to smile about for the home audience. Tossed up, full and around middle and off, Tim Southee gives the charge for a big shot but his bottom hand comes off the handle and the ball flies from the bottom part of his bat. It's a simple catch for Shan Masood at long off. Williamson is 15 away from his double century but is running out of partners now.
Commentary.Howout: c Shan Masood b Nauman Ali

Commentary.Commentary: Short and close to off, Tim cuts but finds point.
Flatter and around leg, Williamson works it through square leg for a single.

Shout for a run out at the bowler's end, taken upstairs. Full and around off, Southee forces it straight back and it kisses the hands of the bowler before going on to break the stumps at the other end. They appeal and the third umpire comes into play. The replays find that Kane has his bat planted inside the crease.
Around off, on a fuller length, Southee defends it to the off side.
Flighted on middle, defended back.
The skipper, Tim Southee walks in.

OUT! CAUGHT! Pakistan have their first wicket of the day but the stand between Ish Sodhi and Kane Williamson has done the damage. Floated delivery, full and on middle at 81.7 kph, Ish Sodhi attempts to take on the leg spinner and tries to heave it across the line. But it comes off from the top half of his blade and flies behind the bowler. Babar Azam is there at mid off and he takes the catch safely. New Zealand lead by 157 runs and still have three wickets remaining.
Commentary.Howout: c Babar Azam b Abrar Ahmed

Commentary.Commentary: On the pads, nudged to square leg for one.

Loopy delivery, full and on middle, Williamson is on the front foot as he defends it to the leg side. He played it alright there as there was a fly that has gone into his eyes while pressing forward in defense.
Spin from both ends as Abrar Ahmed comes into the attack.
Flatter and on the pads, it's tucked away through square leg for a single.
Fuller around leg, Kane defends it off the front foot to point.
Wide! Way down the leg side, no spin there and Williamson leaves. Called a wide.
Fuller and outside leg, Kane keeps his bat away and pads it on the leg side.

EDGY FOUR! Flighted delivery, landing full around leg, Kane Williamson tries to play the reverse sweep out of the rough but it takes the top edge and flies over the leaping slip fielder for a boundary.
Tossed up outside leg, Kane pads it away this time. Pakistan going through the motions now.
Full and flighted, outside leg, Williamson calmly sweeps but finds short fine leg.
Short of a length and on middle, Kane Williamson pulls it towards deep mid-wicket for one. Lead - 150.
Touch fuller and just outside off, Kane Williamson drives it but finds the man at short cover.
Bangs a short ball outside off, Ish Sodhi pulls it and keeps it down. The ball rolls towards deep square leg as the batters collect one.
Bowls it shorter again, Kane Williamson pulls it in front of square on the leg side and picks up another single.
Another shorter one, Ish Sodhi pulls it towards deep square leg for one. This is now Sodhi's highest Test score.
Shorter and on off, Ish Sodhi leaves it alone.
Fuller and on the pads, Kane Williamson sweeps it away to the fielder at short fine leg.
Bowls it on leg, Kane Williamson reverse-sweeps it through point for a brace.
Flighted and outside leg stump, Kane Williamson looks to sweep it but misses.
This one lands outside leg, Kane Williamson pads it away.
Fuller and on the pads, Williamson sweeps it to the short fine leg region.
Fuller and on off, Kane Williamson sweeps it but gets a top edge. The ball lands safely at deep mid-wicket and the batters collect two.
Fuller and on off, Sodhi defends it to the short mid-wicket fielder.
Slightly shorter one, Ish Sodhi flicks it but finds the fielder at short mid-wicket.
Bangs it in short, Sodhi jumps and uses every inch of his height as he defends it down with a loose bottom hand. Has a big smile on his face. Good technique.
Shorter and on off, Kane Williamson gently pulls it to deep mid-wicket for a single.
Bowls it fuller, on middle and leg, Ish Sodhi works it towards mid-wicket for a single.
Shorter and on middle, Ish Sodhi fends it to short leg.
Fuller and down leg, Kane Williamson defends it with his pads again.
Slightly shorter and on middle, Kane Williamson flicks it to the man at short fine leg.
Bowls it outside leg, Kane Williamson pads it away again.
Fuller and outside leg, Kane Williamson sweeps it but finds the man at short fine leg.
Another one outside leg, Kane Williamson defends it with his pads again.
Tossed up, outside leg, Kane Williamson pads it away.
Slightly shorter one, on off. Ish Sodhi defends it back to the bowler.
Fuller one this time, on leg. Ish Sodhi works it straight to the mid-wicket fielder.
Bowls it shorter again, Ish Sodhi ducks underneath it.
Shorter again, on middle. Ish Sodhi fends it back down on the surface.
FOUR! Sodhi has decided to fight fire with fire. Shorter and around off, Ish Sodhi hangs back and pulls it through backward square leg as the ball races away to the fence.

Slight halt in play. The Kiwi physio has come out and he is seen performing the concussion test. Meanwhile, the umpires have decided to take the Drinks break. New Zealand continue to blossom courtesy of this century stand for the seventh wicket and are in firm control. The lead is now 136 runs and Pakistan will be feeling the heat.

Change of plans from Mohammad Wasim and he is having Sodhi in all sorts of trouble. Bangs a bouncer, well-directed, Ish Sodhi looks to pull it but the ball hits his right shoulder and lobs towards the off side at backward point.
Misses again! Nauman continues to bowl full and outside off, Kane initially shapes up for the reverse sweep and then tries to push it away on the leg side but misses. Got into a tangle.
Miscued! Too full and just outside leg, Williamson goes down with the conventional sweep but fails to make connection.
Misses this time! Nauman continues to serves it outside leg, this time Kane fails to connect with his attempted reverse-batted shot.
FOUR! And again, this time in front of square for another boundary. Kane Williamson fetches it from outside leg and reverse-sweeps it firmly to the deep cover fence.
FOUR! Fine execution! Floated delivery, full and close to leg, Kane Williamson brings out the reverse sweep and nails it down to deep backward point for a boundary. Lead - 132.
Loopy and full, landing outside leg, Williamson pads it away.
This is really good from Wasim. Hurls across another short ball around the rib cage of the batter, Sodhi fends it down wide of short leg. End of a probing over.
Good energy on this delivery as well. Short but it's down the leg side, Ish gets across and allows it through to the keeper.

Effort ball from over the wicket. Wasim bangs it in short, around off, Sodhi is taken by surprise and fends it off from the shoulder of his bat. There is no silly point in place otherwise it would have been a simple catch. Now, silly point has come in.
Down the leg side, on a shortish length and staying low, Sodhi tries to pull but it goes below his bat.
Short and around leg, Sodhi is on his toes as he keeps it out to mid on.
Wasim has decided to operate from 'round the wicket. Serves a short ball around off, angling away, Ish Sodhi stays deep inside the crease and allows it through.

Direct hit would have been close! Nauman gives this one some extra air and lands it full around off, Sodhi whips it wide of mid on and scampers across to the other end. Mohammad Wasim has a shy but misses and Ish makes it safely. The replays show that Sodhi would have been a goner in case of a direct hit.
That is defended solidly off the front foot.
Slower through the air this time, around off, Sodhi brings his front foot forward and defends it to the off side.
A touch flatter and around off, Sodhi forces it off the front foot to short cover.
Fuller again, around off, Ish pushes it out off the outer half to point.
Loopy and full, landing around off, Ish Sodhi defends it back.
Wasim is too straight with his line on this occasion and Sodhi works it to deep square leg for a run.
EDGY FOUR! Wasim plants this delivery on a fuller length outside off, Sodhi gets forward to drive away from his body but it catches the outside edge and scoots past gully for a boundary.
Puts it on a fuller length again, around off, once again Sodhi brings a straight bat down in defense.
Fuller and on off, driven off the front foot to covers.
On a good length outside off, Ish stays back and plays it down to point.
Begins with a full ball on off, angling in, Sodhi plays it nice and late as he defends it ahead of his front pad.
Mohammad Wasim (29-5-90-1) comes into the attack now.
Slower through the air, outside off and breaking away a bit late, Williamson fiddles with it, inside the line and gets beaten.

FOUR! Fantastic shot! Kane Williamson has looked in control whenever he has advanced down the track. Full and flighted, around off and turning away, Williamson shimmies down and lofts it over mid on for a boundary. Lead - 122.
Loopy and around off, turning away, Williamson defends it away with gentle hands on the off side.
FOUR! Played well in the end. Another arm ball, around middle and leg and staying low, Kane does well to stands back and nudge it fine down the leg side for a boundary at fine leg.
Arm ball around leg, Ish tries to flick but misses. It goes off his pads to short fine leg and they cross for a leg bye.
Tossed up, full and on off, Ish defends it back.

FOUR! Fuller and outside off, Kane Williamson strides forward to defend it but gets a thick outside edge as the ball goes past the first slip fielder, and through to the third-man fence. Lucky boundary!
This one lands on off, Kane Williamson defends it back towards the bowler.
Skidding away on leg, Ish works it to deep square leg for a single.
Fuller and on middle, Ish Sodhi tucks it to the man at mid-wicket.

Miscommunication but no harm is done. Slower one, on leg. Ish Sodhi pushes it towards short mid-wicket and looks for a run. He is midway down the track but Kane Williamson shouts a big NO and sends him back. The bowler gets to the ball and fires in a throw but it's a bit weak and Ish returns with a clumsy dive. Williamson is now seen having a word with his partner.
Tossed up, on middle, Ish Sodhi lunges and blocks it to mid off.
Another fuller one, down leg. Kane Williamson flicks it straight to the man at square leg.
Fuller and on off, Kane Williamson defends it back towards the bowler.

FOUR! Good-length delivery, outside off. Kane Williamson uses the pace of the ball and just guides it through to third man for a boundary. 150 up for Kane Williamson, this is the 9th time he has done so in Test cricket!
On a length and outside off, shaping away a touch. Kane Williamson looks to block it but misses.
Fuller and on off, Ish Sodhi pushes it towards the right of mid on for a single.
Around the wicket. Length ball, outside off. Ish Sodhi pushes it towards point.
Fuller and down leg, Ish Sodhi looks to flick it but gets a rap on his pads. It rolls towards the leg side as the batters cross for a leg bye.
Fuller and on off, Ish Sodhi pushes it to covers.

FOUR! Fifty up for Ish Sodhi. This is fuller and outside off, Ish Sodhi uses the pace of the ball and guides it through to third man for a boundary. 4th fifty in Tests for Ish Sodhi and the lead has also gone over 100.
Bowls it fuller and on off, Ish Sodhi eases it to the man at point.
Shorter and on off, Kane Williamson cuts it through covers for one.
FOUR! Fine shot. Slightly shorter one, on middle, slower too. Kane Williamson rocks back and pulls it through the square leg region for a boundary.
Fuller one, angling in. Ish Sodhi defends off the front foot down to mid off.
Fuller and just outside off, Ish Sodhi blocks it to short cover.
Touch fuller and outside off, shaping away. Kane Williamson looks to defend it with soft hands but gets an inside edge as the ball rolls towards short fine leg. They cross.
On a length and on middle, Kane Williamson tucks it towards mid-wicket for a brace. Good running between the wickets.
Full-length delivery, angling in from outside off. Kane Williamson drives it but finds the man at covers.
On a length and on middle, Kane Williamson defends it solidly towards mid on.
FOUR! Connects well this time. Tossed up, wide outside off. Ish Sodhi hangs back and slashes it through backward point for a boundary.
Another one outside off with some turn, Ish Sodhi looks to slap it but misses.
This one lands outside off, Ish Sodhi looks to cut it but misses.
Fuller and on off, Kane Williamson moves forward and drives it uppishly towards deep extra cover for one.
Bowls it on middle, Kane Williamson hangs back and blocks it towards the bowler.
Over the wicket. Bowls it fuller and on off, Kane Williamson lunges and blocks it to short cover.
A bit short in length and outside off, going straight on, Sodhi remains on the back foot and lets it be.
On a length and close to off, Williamson plays it down to the left side of the cover fielder and pinches a single.
Fuller and around off, defended back.
Back of a length, around off, Kane goes on the back foot and taps it down on the surface.
Down the leg side, Ish tickles it behind square leg for a run.
Angles in a length ball on off, Sodhi stays back and helps it off his pads to short mid-wicket.
Mir Hamza to bowl from the other end.
Gets behind the line of the delivery and pushes it with hard hands, back to the bowler.
Fullish around off, turning in, the batter has just watchfully blocked this out.
Slightly fuller on off, Kane gets forward and pushes it to covers.
Shortish and on off, punched off the back foot to mid on.
Flighted and full, around off, Kane is on the front foot in defense.
Runs straightaway although leg byes. Skidding down the leg side, Williamson tries to sweep but misses. It deflects off his pads to fine leg for two leg byes.

We are back for the second session of Day 4. The umpires and the players have made their way out in the middle. Kane Williamson and Ish Sodhi will resume their innings. Meanwhile, Agha Salman is back on the field. Abrar Ahmed to start from this end. Here we go...
... DAY 4, SESSION 2 ...

It was a slow session in terms of the scoring rate and you can expect New Zealand to press on the accelerator at some point in time in the afternoon session. Pakistan have played all their cards but without any success. Had they been more alert, they could have cashed in on those missed opportunities. Let's see how the second session pans out which will start at 1.10 pm IST (7.40 am GMT).

The morning session belonged to New Zealand! They have not run away with the show but have stretched their lead to 81 runs. It was a cautious approach from them and that's why we didn't see anything reckless from the pair of Kane Williamson and Ish Sodhi. The latter, in particular, has faced 127 balls now for his 41 and never looked much in trouble. There were a couple of moments when he nicked but the keeper didn't take the catch and then when he nicked again, no one appealed from Pakistan. He has had his slice of luck and New Zealand have put themselves in the driving seat.
Flighted and full, around off, Sodhi defends it off the front foot to covers. That will be LUNCH ON DAY 4!
Ball number 165.2 - The UltraEdge again detects a spike. But no one appealed. Another chance goes begging for Pakistan.
Gets on the front foot and defends it back to the bowler.
Fuller and around leg, Sodhi turns it calmly to short leg.
Very full and on off, Sodhi digs it out to point.
Turning in from around off, Sodhi helps it off his pads to mid-wicket.
Fullish and on middle, defended back safely.
The skipper, Babar Azam to bowl the last over before Lunch.
Flatter and in line with the stumps, Williamson is on the back foot in defense.
Gentle hands. Full again, on off, Williamson pushes it off the front foot to covers.
Full and around off, staying low, Kane moves back and pushes it to point.
Skidding in around off, Williamson goes back and keeps it away off the inner edge. It goes wide of short leg.
Floated and full, drifting in around middle, Kane flicks it towards short leg.
Flighted delivery, on middle, Sodhi works it towards short fine leg and takes a single.
Delivers it full and outside off, Kane gets forward and drives it in the gap at sweeper cover for two runs.
Back of a length around off, holding its line a touch, Williamson hangs his bat out pointlessly and it whistles past the outside edge.
Well played! A length ball around off, Sodhi wrists it through square leg and rotates the strike.
FOUR! That's a nice shot. Full in length outside off, inviting the drive, Sodhi reaches out and strokes it through the gap at covers for a boundary.
Beaten! Hamza pitches it up and outside off, Sodhi pushes inside the line and misses.
Hurls across a length ball around off, angling in from 'round the wicket, Williamson remains on the back foot and guides it through point for a single.
Slightly shorter one, on off. Ish Sodhi eases it to the fielder at short cover.
Fuller one and on middle, Ish Sodhi lunges and offers a dead bat to it.
Another one on middle, Ish Sodhi again defends it towards the bowler.
Fuller and on middle, Ish Sodhi defends it back towards the bowler.

FOUR! Slightly shorter and outside off, Ish Sodhi hangs back and cuts it through covers as the ball races away to the fence. Hasan Ali gives the chase but he loses the battle as the ball teasingly goes to the fence.
Tossed up, outside off, turning away. Kane Williamson slaps it to deep cover for a single.
Fuller one, angling in, Ish Sodhi reads it well and blocks it to short cover.
A yorker right into the blockhole, Ish Sodhi digs it to the man at point.

EDGED AND FOUR! On a length with some extra bounce, outside off. Ish Sodhi opens the face of the bat and looks to guide it but gets a thick outside edge as the ball races away to the third man fence. Lucky boundary!
Bowls it fuller and just outside off, Kane Williamson drives it towards deep cover for a single.
Touch fuller and outside leg, Kane Williamson looks to tickle it but misses.
This one lands outside leg, shaping away, Kane Williamson leaves the harmless delivery.
Outside off, blocked at mid off.
Fuller and on middle, this is pushed to the man at point.
Outside off, this is played towards covers for a single. 500 comes up!
Short of a length and on off, Kane Williamson eases it to the point fielder.
Fuller and on leg,  Sodhi tucks it away to short fine leg for a single.
Fuller on the stumps, Sodhi defends it back to the bowler.
Another fuller one as this is again defended towards the bowler.
Fuller one as this is defended back towards the bowler.
Fuller on the stumps, Williamson defends it to the mid-wicket region.
Fuller and on leg, Sodhi looks to flick it but misses as the ball hits his pads and rolls towards the leg side. They cross for a leg bye.
FOUR! Short and wide outside off, Sodhi cuts it away through the point region and the ball races away to the fence in no time.
Fuller and on off, Sodhi defends it away.
Around leg, defended.
The reserve umpire has tossed up the third new ball to one of the on-field umpires. Pakistan have opted for it and it's going to be Mir Hamza to make the first use of it.
Fuller and outside leg, Kane Williamson pads it away.
Goes for the reverse sweep but misses the ball here as it goes towards the keeper.
Fuller and on leg, Kane Williamson reverse-sweeps it to deep cover for a brace.

Five penalty runs! Flighted delivery, down the leg side, Williamson tries to sweep but misses. Sarfaraz Ahmed fails to grab and it goes through his legs to hit the helmet kept behind him on the ground. The lead crosses 50!
Pitches this outside the leg stump, Kane Williamson pads it away.
This one lands outside leg, Kane Williamson looks to reverse-sweep it but misses.
Short and on off, Ish punches but finds the fielder at cover-point. The third new ball is due now.
Full around off, the batter has just blocked that from his crease.
Gets behind the line of the delivery and defends it back.
Quicker and on off, defended from the back foot.
Around off, driven through covers for a single. The 50-run stand comes up!
Ball number 158.2 - The UltraEdge shows that there was a spike. So that will go down as a dropped catch.
Tossed up around middle, defended on the leg side.
Flatter and around leg, Sodhi defends it with the turn to the off side.
Flighted and outside leg, Sodhi pads it away with ease.
Superbly executed. Full and flighted, outside leg, Kane Williamson reverse-sweeps out of the rough and sends it to deep cover. They get three runs.
Loopy and full, around leg and spinning away viciously, Sodhi is beaten as he prods forward to defend. Sarfaraz Ahmed fails to collect and they steal a bye.
Mir Hamza is warming up. The third new ball is due shortly.
Down the leg side, Ish tries to flick but misses. Sarfaraz Ahmed fails to gather the ball cleanly.
Ali continues to target the rough outside leg, the length is a bit short this time and Kane nudges it wide of short fine leg for a run.
Serves it around off, Sodhi stays back and punches it towards the bowler.
Fires it full and around leg, again Ish defends it from deep inside the crease.
Flatter and on off, defended off the back foot again.
Nicely flighted around off, a touch short in length, Ish gets back and defends it.
Quicker and shorter on off, Kane moves back and punches it to deep cover for a single.
Slow spin away from the batter around off, Williamson plays late with soft hands but fails to beat the first slip fielder.
Floated around leg, too full in length, it's defended back to the bowler.
FOUR! Well played! Nauman is a bit on the shorter side, landing around leg and turning away a shade, Sodhi uses the depth of his crease and spanks it through covers.
Beauty to beat the bat! Floated one, full and landing in the rough outside leg, Sodhi lunges to defend but it beats the bat and goes just over the top of the off stump. Nauman is in disbelief.
Quicker and very full outside leg, Sodhi steps back and drives it to mid off.
Another delivery landing in the rough outside leg, Sodhi tries to pad it away again but misses. A good take by Sarfaraz Ahmed.
Tossed up outside leg, Sodhi pads it away.
Gets forward to a full ball and pushes it softly to short cover.
Around leg, full in length, Kane helps it to mid-wicket.
Flatter and shorter on off, punched off the back foot to covers.
Quicker and around leg, it's worked to deep square leg for a couple of runs.

Aerial but again the batter is safe. Loopy delivery, full and around off, Sodhi top-edges his attempted sweep and looks down in disappointment. It flies to the right of short fine leg and falls safely. They get a run.

We are all set for the game to begin. The umpires have made their way out in the middle. The Pakistan players are seen in a huddle near the ropes. Kane Williamson and Ish Sodhi will resume their innings. Mohammad Wasim to start from this end. Here we go...

Tom Latham comes up for a chat! The opener starts by admitting that he was not aware of the milestone he achieved (the most hundreds by a Kiwi opener). Shares that heading into the series they had a close look at how this particular pitch has played in the recent past and prepared accordingly. Feels that the pitch has started to throw up tricks and they needed to adjust to it. Adds that sweeping from the rough, with the spin, was a better option for him and it turned out to be quite productive.

Pakistan clawed their way back into the game late on Day 3. Mohammad Wasim got rid of Tom Blundell and Michael Bracewell soon followed. The hosts were too clumsy with their fielding and had their fielding been on point, they could have ended New Zealand's innings by now. Pakistan will need to improve on their fielding now and bag some early wickets this morning. Can they do it? Or will the New Zealand batters stretch their lead? We shall find out shortly. Stay tuned...

Starting the day at 165 for no loss, the visitors started off slow but lost Devon Conway early on at 183. Tom Latham continued his good work and notched up his 13th Test century and added 48 runs for the second wicket alongside Kane Williamson. Latham then lost his wicket but Williamson continued to bat. He then survived a couple of stumpings, thanks to Sarfaraz Ahmed's failed glovework, and made Pakistan pay for it with a lovely hundred. New Zealand are now 2 runs ahead and they will be eyeing a handy lead.

Hello and a warm welcome to Day 4 of the New Zealand tour of Pakistan. All three days were unpredictable and the momentum swung from one end to another like in pendulum for both sides. For now, New Zealand have a slight upper hand in the game with Williamson still batting on 105* and the Kiwis having a lead of 2 runs with 4 wickets in the bank. Nonetheless, some quick wickets at the start now can get Pakistan back on level terms.
... DAY 4, SESSION 1 ...

The 'moving day' comes to a close but this Test match has not moved a lot. It's delicately poised and heading more towards a one-inning shootout. Williamson has some capable batters to come and New Zealand will be hoping that they gain a handy lead in the first innings. For Pakistan, it's all about picking the remaining four wickets quickly and then batting with a more sensible approach. This pitch is only going to get tougher for batting, mainly due to the variable bounce. A couple of exciting days in store. Do join us on Day 4 at 10.30 am IST (5 am GMT) for all the action. Until then, it's goodbye and cheers!

Pakistan bowled with all their heart and soul. At times, they looked threatening with their spinners but the consistency factor was lacking. Add to it, they were quite clumsy in the field as well. Not to forget the missed stumping chance of Kane Williamson when he was on 21 and just like Babar Azam, he is also making the opposition pay for that error.

It won't be wrong to say that Day 3 belonged to both teams! They shared the honours. Pakistan were impressive in the morning session as they removed both the openers and kept things tight as well by giving away only 80 runs. New Zealand felt the pressure but never allowed Pakistan to run away with the show. Apart from one occasion, every time when a wicket fell, there was a partnership and Kane Williamson was the linchpin. He completed his 25th Test hundred and threaded quite a few stands. In the afternoon session, when the hosts were planning to dominate, the knock of Daryl Mitchell proved to be very vital, as his positive approach wrestled the momentum back in New Zealand's corner.

End of an excellent day of Test cricket where the momentum swung like a pendulum. A couple of late wickets in the day for Pakistan, and because of that, they have not allowed New Zealand to gain the upper hand in the game. For most parts of the final session, Kane Williamson and Tom Blundell successfully dealt with everything thrown at them and formed a 90-run alliance. Blundell lived dangerously during his stay but eventually fell three short of his fifty.

Imam from mid on and Abrar Ahmed from mid off charge for it but then they both pull off, leaving it for each other. The batters get two runs. Imam-ul-Haq later gestures that he wanted to dive but then pulled off seeing Abrar. Hmm... there was on calling!
Flighted around leg, Blundell gets forward and defends it to the leg side.
Extra turn and bounce from around leg, Blundell gets back to defend but misses and is hit on the back thigh.
Full again, on off and reversing back into the batter, Kane helps it to mid-wicket to complete the over.
Fuller and on off, shaping in a bit, Blundell drives it from the inner half and it goes straight down the ground. They cross for a run.
Drifting down the leg side, a length ball, Tom Blundell clips it through square leg and shouts 'push-push'. They do push hard and complete the second run.
Lands it on a length outside off, Williamson pushes it with an angled bat through cover-point for a single.
Back of a length around off, Kane stays on the back foot and blocks it to covers.
A length ball on off, angling into the batter, Williamson plays it with soft hands and pushes it to mid-wicket.
Puts it on a fuller length around off, Blundell comes down with a little shimmy and then defends it.
Loopy and full around leg, Blundell draws forward and defends again.
Fuller around middle and leg, the batter has just watchfully blocked this out.
Fuller and around leg, swept to deep square leg for a single.
Identical to the last delivery, Kane stretches forward and blocks it safely.
Flighted and full around leg, Williamson defends it off the front foot.
On a length and on middle, Tom Blundell turns it to short leg.
Good-length delivery, on middle and leg, Tom Blundell defends it solidly.

Fuller and on middle and leg, Kane Williamson drills it down the ground. The fielder, Shan Masood, has a long chase and he stops it just before the fence by sliding. The batters collect three. With those three runs, New Zealand cross the 400-run mark.
Fuller and outside off, Tom Blundell looks to play at it but gets an inside edge as the ball rolls towards leg slip. They collect one.
Angles in a length ball around middle, Tom Blundell looks to defend it but gets an inside edge onto the pads as the ball rolls towards point. The bowler gets excited for a moment.
Bowls it fuller and on middle, Tom Blundell digs it towards mid on. Dot.
Another one skidding away from outside leg, Kane Williamson pads it away once more.
This one lands outside off, Kane Williamson leaves it alone.
Keeps it bowling down leg, Kane Williamson puts his pads forward as the ball lobs up towards slips.
Another one down leg, Kane Williamson defends it with his pads.
Fuller and down leg, Tom Blundell moves forward to flick it but miscues it to cover-point. They cross.
Tossed up, down leg, Tom Blundell pads it away.
Fuller one on off, Kane Williamson defends it to silly mid off. Ends the over with a dot.
Good-length delivery, angling in. Kane Williamson offers a dead bat to it.
Bowls it fuller this time, on leg. Tom Blundell works it towards square leg for a single.
Another one on a length, shaping in. Tom Blundell taps it to the man at extra cover.
On a length, angling in. Tom Blundell blocks it back towards the bowler.
Slightly shorter and on off, Tom Blundell fends it to short covers.
Mohammad Wasim comes back into the attack. 0 for 62 in his 16 overs so far. Pakistan are lacking the fifth bowling option with Agha Salman going off the field again.
This one lands outside leg, Kane Williamson looks to defend it with his pads but misses.
Bowls it on middle, Tom Blundell looks to flick it but miscues it to covers off the leading half. They cross.
Tossed up, on middle. Tom Blundell lunges and defends it back towards the bowler.
Bowls it on middle, Tom Blundell eases it to the man at mid on.
Another one outside leg, Tom Blundell defends it with his pads again.
Tosses it up down leg, Tom Blundell pads it away.
Fuller and on middle and leg, Tom Blundell flicks it to mid on for one more.
Bowls it on off, Kane Williamson drills it to long on for one.
This one lands down leg, Kane Williamson looks to flick it but gets a rap on his pads and it bounces off the deck. Dot.
Another fuller one, on middle, Kane Williamson flicks it but finds the man at mid-wicket.
This one lands on off, Kane Williamson blocks it back towards the bowler.
FOUR! Superbly executed! Fuller and on off, Kane Williamson dances down the track and lofts it over mid off for a boundary.
Bowls it full and around off, Tom walks forward and then checks his shot. He defends it to covers.
Slower through the air, full and on off, Blundell defends it from the inner half of his bat.

In the air but safe! Floated delivery, full and around leg, Williamson tries to sweep out of the rough but gets a top edge. It flies behind short fine leg and they cross for a run. The deficit now is 50.
Full and outside leg, Williamson pads it away.

Well stopped by Zahid Mahmood (sub)! Fuller and on middle, Blundell whips it across the line and Zahid reacts quickly to his right from mid on. He dives to stop the racing ball and saves three runs. The 50-run stand comes up.
A shade flatter and shorter on off, Tom Blundell defends it back from the back foot.
Slightly short and on middle, Blundell moves back and forces it down to mid on for a single.
Loopy and full, around off, Tom defends off the front foot.
Shortish and on middle, punched off the back foot to mid-wicket.
FOUR! Smacked! Tossed up, full and around middle, Tom Blundell jumps down the track and drills it past his partner at the other end for a boundary at long on.
Quicker through the air, again a bit short, Blundell pushes it back from the crease.
Going straight on after landing around off, Blundell defends it from the back foot.
Fullish and landing outside leg, once again Kane uses his front pad to keep it out.
Nauman comes from over the wicket and delivers a full ball outside leg on the rough. Williamson pads it away.

Mistimed once more! Nauman Ali serves a full ball around leg and gets it to straighten from there, Tom Blundell plays the line and tries to flick but it takes the leading edge and scoots wide of first slip. They cross.
Full in length around middle, Blundell lunges shows the full face of his bat in defense.

Miscues again! Full and floated around off, Tom Blundell skips down the track to heave it over the leg side but ends up dragging it off the inner edge. The ball dribbles behind square leg for a couple of runs.
Skidding down the leg side, Blundell tries to flick but misses.
Flighted delivery, pitching quite full outside off, Williamson presses forward and jams it down.
Shortish and on off, Kane goes back and pushes it to covers.
Extra flight this time, full and drifting in around off, Williamson is forward as he defends it to short leg.
Googly around off, on the shorter side, Tom punches it from the back foot to extra cover for one.
Fullish and around off, Blundell lunges and defends it back.
Flatter one on off, Blundell goes on the back foot and defends.

Streaky. Fuller and on off, turning away, Tom Blundell again advances down the track to flick it across the line but it takes the leading edge and goes in the air. It's again in the gap at covers and they cross.
The batter has just watchfully blocked this out.

Fuller and on off, Tom hurries down the track and drills it straight back. Nauman Ali goes down to stop the ball but it brushes his right hand and sneaks past the stumps at the other end as Kane turns to plant his bat inside the crease. Blundell shows interest in a run but Kane Williamson sends him back.
Slower one, full and floated on middle, Blundell is forward as he defends it back.
Allows the ball to come close to his body and nudges it towards fine leg for a single.
Flatter and on middle, Kane works off his pads but finds short leg.
SIX! Sweetly connected. Fuller and on middle, Tom Blundell dances down the track and heaves it over deep mid-wicket for a maximum.
Slower one on off, Tom Blundell blocks it back.
Goes fuller and on off, Tom Blundell defends it back towards the bowler.
Bowls it outside off, Tom Blundell drives but finds the fielder at covers.
Slightly shorter one, Tom Blundell hangs back and blocks it back towards the bowler.
Bowls it on leg, Kane Williamson flicks it to backward square leg for one.
Full and on the stumps. Tom Blundell blocks it back at the bowler off the front foot.

In the air but lands safely. Fuller and on off, turning away a shade with some extra bounce, Tom Blundell advances down the track for a lofted shot but slices it towards extra cover. Wasim runs across to his left from mid off but it drops in front of him. He tries to collect it on the bounce but instead kicks it away with his right leg. The batters get the chance to complete the second run.
Flatter and on middle, Tom Blundell shuffles across and eases it to covers.
Fuller and on leg, Kane Williamson flicks it to square leg for one.
This was similar to the last delivery, Kane Williamson again defends it back towards the bowler.
Fuller and on middle, Kane Williamson lunges and blocks it back towards the bowler.
This one lands outside off, Tom Blundell blocks it to covers.
Tossed up, on middle. This is defended back towards the bowler.
This one lands on off, Tom Blundell defends it towards mid off.
FOUR! Slightly shorter and on off, Tom Blundell looks to slap it but gets a bottom edge as the ball goes past the keeper and Mohammad Wasim (chasing from short fine leg) for a boundary.
Tossed up, with some turn. Tom Blundell looks to defend it but gets an inside edge onto the pads.
Drags his length short and bowls it outside off, Tom cuts but finds the fielder at backward point.
Quicker one on middle, Kane Williamson looks to defend it but gets an inside edge to square leg.
FOUR! Excellent footwork. Fuller and on middle, Kane Williamson uses his feet and lofts it over the bowler for a boundary.
Bowls it outside off, Tom Blundell steers it to point for one.
Slightly shorter one, Blundell defends off the back foot to the right of the bowler.
Fuller again, on middle. Tom Blundell lunges and blocks it to point.
Tossed up, on middle. Tom Blundell eases it to mid off.
Spin from both ends after the break. Nauman Ali (28-1-106-2) comes back into the attack.
Slightly shorter and outside off, Kane Williamson guides it towards the man at backward point. Ends with a dot.
Slower one on leg, Tom Blundell flicks it to backward square leg for one.
Fuller and on middle and leg, Kane Williamson works it to square leg for one.
Tossed up, on middle. Kane Williamson lunges and blocks it away.
Slightly shorter and on middle, slower too. Tom Blundell hangs back and punches it to mid off for a quick single.
Bowls it fuller and on middle and leg, Tom Blundell defends it to mid on.

We are back for the final session of Day 3. The umpires have made their way out in the middle. The Pakistan players are seen in a huddle near the ropes. Kane Williamson and Tom Blundell will resume their innings. Abrar Ahmed to start from this end. Here we go.
... DAY 3, SESSION 3 ...

Right then, the deficit for New Zealand is 85 runs and this Test match is more or less in the balance. The tourists still have six wickets in hand and the presence of Kane Williamson will be giving them a lot of assurance. Pakistan had the opportunity to remove him on 21 but Sarfaraz Ahmed missed the stumping opportunity. 37 overs left in the day's play and by the end of it, we could get some hint about which way this Test match will head. Do join us at 3.30 pm IST (10 am GMT) for the final session.

The pendulum swings again in this Test match! Pakistan had started to gain control after an excellent morning session, but New Zealand refused to go down. Despite losing Henry Nicholls, the tourists stayed focused, and the arrival of Daryl Mitchell only injected more intent into their innings. He constructed a quick stand with Kane Williamson before getting out but the former Kiwi skipper is still going strong and looking good for a big one. Pakistan's bowling was decent but they didn't threaten the way we expected them to in the afternoon session.
Another length ball angling in from around off, Kane Williamson defends it as well to end the session. TEA ON DAY 3!
Close to off, full and angling in, Williamson plays near his body and defends it to the off side.
In the zone outside off, on a length, Williamson shoulders arms.
Full and on off, Kane defends it back.
FOUR! Easy pickings! Wasim lands it on a length, around middle and leg, Williamson waits and deflects it neatly off his pads to fine leg for a boundary.
Uses the angle of the bowler and works a full ball to mid-wicket.
Fuller on middle, defended towards short leg again.
Googly around off, fuller in length, Blundell lunges to defend and does so off the inside edge. It rolls to short leg.
Flatter and on middle, skidding in, Kane nudges it behind square leg for a run.
Slower through the air, full and on off, Williamson draws forward and defends. It hits the shoulder of his bat and rolls back, beats the stumps by not much.
Quicker through the air, a bit short and on middle, Kane gets back and wrists it through mid-wicket for a couple of runs.
Loopy and full on off, Williamson presses forward and blocks it to the off side.
Lands it on a length, around off, Blundell gets forward and defends it to the off side.
Full again, around off, Blundell gets behind the line and defends it towards silly mid on.
Fuller and on off, Tom drives it down the ground and Kane Williamson jumps to make way. It though goes straight to the fielder at mid on.
Pitches it up and around off, Tom Blundell meets it with a dead bat in defense.
A length ball on off, Williamson uses the angle and tickles it through backward square leg for a single.
Fractionally short from Wasim, around off, Williamson is on the back foot in defense.
Abrar drops it short around off, Blundell gets back and punches it towards cover-point.
Fuller and on off, easily defended off the front foot by Tom.
Floated delivery, full and on off, Blundell defends it ahead of his front pad.
Leans forward to a full ball and drives it through covers for a run.
Slightly short and on leg, Williamson gets back and works it to deep mid-wicket for a couple of runs.
Flighted and full on middle, Williamson lunges and defends it off the inner half to short leg.
Another delivery in the region outside off, Blundell covers his stumps and makes another leave.
Outside off, left alone.
In the channel outside off, on a good length, Tom Blundell shoulders arms.
Full and around off, angling away, Tom is batting outside his crease, and he defends it with ease.
On a length around middle, defended from the back foot.
FOUR! Lovely shot! Full in length and outside off, Tom Blundell leans forward and crunches it through point for a boundary. The deficit is below 100 now.
Touch fuller and on leg, Kane Williamson hangs back and blocks it back towards the bowler.
Fuller and on middle, Tom Blundell flicks it towards square leg and gets off the mark. They cross.
Tom Blundell walks in next. New Zealand trail by 101 runs.

OUT! CAUGHT! Another Kiwi batter falls gloving his attempted reverse sweep. Abrar tosses it up around off, gets a hint of turn with some extra bounce, Daryl Mitchell looks to play the reverse batted shot but fails to connect and the ball hits his gloves. It lobs up in the air and Sarfaraz Ahmed moves forward to take a simple catch. The bowler had turned to appeal for an lbw but then found out that it was off the gloves and caught. The finger is up and Daryl Mitchell starts to walk. Kane Williamson just checks with him whether he is sure, Mitchell nods and returns.
Commentary.Howout: c Sarfaraz Ahmed b Abrar Ahmed

Fuller and on middle, Kane Williamson flicks it towards square leg for one.
Beaten! Ahmed delivers it full and around off, Williamson gets forward to defend the line but it spins away to beat the outside edge.
Agha Salman is on the field now. He was also down with flu, just like Babar Azam.
This one lands outside off, Daryl Mitchell prods forward and defends it firmly down to short cover. Ends with a dot.
On a length and on off, Mitchell flicks it but finds the man at mid-wicket.
Length ball on off. Mitchell defends off the front foot towards mid off.
Bowls it fuller and on middle, Daryl Mitchell blocks it back towards the bowler.
Another one outside off, shaping away. Daryl Mitchell shoulders arms at it.
Good-length delivery, outside off, shaping away. Daryl Mitchell lets it through towards the keeper.
Fuller and on off, Kane Williamson stands tall and defends it solidly.
Slightly shorter and on the pads, Williamson tucks it to short leg.
Fuller and on off, Kane Williamson defends it solidly.
Bowls it on middle, Daryl Mitchell looks to loft it but the ball hits the inside half of his bat and carries towards the right of mid on. It lands safely as the batters collect one.
This one lands on middle and leg, Kane Williamson tucks it to square leg for one.
Bowls it fuller and on off, Kane Williamson eases it to the man at mid off.
Abrar Ahmed comes back into the attack, this time from the University End. 32-3-105-1 are his figures so far.
Fuller and just outside off, Daryl Mitchell prods forward and defends it to mid off.
This one lands on middle and leg, Daryl Mitchell offers a dead bat to it.
Touch fuller this time, Kane Williamson drives it to deep cover for one.
Bowls it outside off, shaping it away, Kane Williamson leaves the harmless delivery.
On a length again with some extra bounce, Kane Williamson blocks it solidly towards mid off.
On a length and outside off, shaping away a touch, Kane Williamson looks to defend it but gets beaten on the outside edge.
Touch fuller and outside off, Daryl Mitchell drives it to the point region.
Bowls it on off, Daryl Mitchell looks to drive it but miscues it to the man at mid on. Dot.
Keeps it bowling fuller in length, Kane Williamson nudges it to deep mid-wicket for a single.
Fuller and on off, Daryl Mitchell eases it towards covers for a single.
FOUR! Sublime timing. Mohammad Wasim goes fuller this time, Daryl Mitchell flicks it and times it perfectly through mid-wicket for a boundary.
Good-length delivery, angling in. Daryl Mitchell defends it back towards the bowler.
Bowls it in the line of the stumps, on a length, Williamson stays on the back foot and dead-bats it near the surface.
Pitches it up and around off, Kane Williamson drives but the cover fielder is alert and stops the ball.
On a good length around middle and off, Kane defends from the back foot.
Hamza again keeps it full and lands ti wide outside off, Williamson tries to drive but it takes the inner half and rolls back to the bowler.
Delivers it full and on off, Williamson drives but finds the fielder at short cover.
Serves it on a length around off, shaping back in a hint, Williamson covers his stumps and allows it through.
Wasim goes fuller and on off, Daryl is forward as he meets it with a straight bat in defense. Maiden!
This one is on a driving length outside off, Mitchell doesn't accept the proposal and allows it through to the keeper.
Lands it on a good length around off, Mitchell goes on the back foot and defends it to the off side.
Close to off, full and angling in, Mitchell defends it near his front pad.
Fuller and on off, again Daryl Mitchell plays a lovely off drive but only to find the fielder.
Daryl Mitchell is timing his shots brilliantly. This time though it is not in the gap. Full and outside off, it's driven to mid off.
Full and around off, angling away, Williamson covers the stumps and shoulders arms.
On a good length around off, Williamson goes on the back foot in defense.

Delivers it on a length outside off, angling away, Mitchell plays inside the line and guides it past gully for a couple of runs.

Fuller delivery, around middle, Williamson gets behind the line and defends it back.

Drinks! The Kiwi batters are looking to stitch a new partnership after the dismissal of Henry Nicholls. They have just been brutal against the Pakistani bowlers. Daryl Mitchell is playing with more aggressive intent than Kane Williamson, who is hanging on with him. 78 runs came in the last hour and the Kiwis are wrestling back the momentum. Mir Hamza to bowl after the break.

FOUR! Fourth boundary in a row and the 50-run stand comes up in no time. Fuller in length around middle and leg, Daryl Mitchell unfurls a beautiful on-drive and fetches another boundary. He is on fire and the deficit is down to 115 runs.

FOUR! Little streaky on this occasion. Wasim delivers it on a length and close to off, Mitchell tries to push inside the line and edges it. The ball races down to third man for a boundary. Three in a row!
FOUR! Daryl Mitchell has come out with attacking intent. Short in length and wide outside off, Mitchell rocks back and smacks it through point for a boundary.
FOUR! This partnership continues to blossom at a brilliant rate. A low full toss on off, at 131.1 kph, Daryl Mitchell strides forward and drives it firmly down the ground for a boundary at long off.
Hurls it across on a length and quite outside off at 129.7 kph, Daryl Mitchell shoulders arms.
Wasim runs in from over the wicket and serves it full around off, Daryl drives it off the front foot to mid off.
Mohammad Wasim comes into the attack now.
This one goes straight on from around off, Kane goes back in defense.
Extra flight there as it lands full around off, Mitchell wrists it to wide mid on for a single.
FIFTY! Quicker and shorter on off, Williamson goes on the back foot and forces it through point for a single. This is his 34th fifty in Tests. A fine knock from the former skipper.
Fuller and on off, defended with a dead bat.
Tossed up around off, defended back.
FOUR! Williamson continues to target the mid-wicket region. Short and on middle, Kane waits on the back foot for a fraction longer and whips it through mid-wicket for a boundary. Moves to 49!
Slightly shorter, turning away from the right-hander, Kane Williamson hangs back and guides it late past first slip and backward point. Gets a single.
Bowls it on middle and leg, Daryl Mitchell flicks it towards mid on for a single. 300 comes up for New Zealand!
Another one on off, fuller in length. Daryl Mitchell prods forward and defends it to mid off.
Bowls it on off, Daryl Mitchell defends it to mid on.
Goes fuller and on off, Daryl Mitchell lunges and blocks it away.

FOUR! Doesn't time it well but gets the result he wanted. This one lands fuller and on middle and leg, Daryl Mitchell uses his feet and lofts it over mid on, from the inside half of his bat, and gets a boundary.
Another fuller one, Kane Williamson lunges and defends it back towards the bowler.
Fuller and on off, Kane Williamson blocks it watchfully.
FOUR! Even better! Again Abrar delivers it a bit short on middle, staying low, Kane gets low in his stance and through his wonderful wrists, he flicks it to deep mid-wicket for a boundary.
This one lands on off, Kane Williamson defends it to mid on.

FOUR! Timing of the highest order! A touch short and on middle, turning away, Williamson goes on the back foot and works it with sublime timing through mid-wicket. It keeps on running away from the chasing fielder and finds the fence.
Bowls it on middle and leg, Kane Williamson blocks it solidly off the front foot.
Ali goes fuller again, on middle. Daryl Mitchell defends it back towards the bowler.
Another one on off, fuller in length. Daryl Mitchell leans forward and blocks it to silly point.
Bowls it on off, Daryl Mitchell eases it to the man at mid off.
This one lands on off, Daryl Mitchell lunges and defends it this time.

SIX! All the way. This is how he will approach his inning against the spinners, in particular. Fuller and on middle, Daryl Mitchell shimmies down the wicket and powers it over long on for a maximum. Excellent use of the feet.
Around the wicket. Fuller and on off, Daryl Mitchell lunges and blocks it away.

Slower one, on middle. Kane Williamson hangs back and blocks it back towards the bowler.
Tossed up, on off. Daryl Mitchell knocks it towards mid on for one.
Fuller and on off, Daryl Mitchell defends it solidly.
FOUR! Excellent timing on this. Fuller and on middle, Daryl Mitchell reads it well and plays a reverse sweep through point for a boundary. Gets off the mark.
Bowls it fuller and on middle, Daryl Mitchell lunges and defends it back towards the bowler. No ball is called for overstepping.

Daryl Mitchell is the new batter. He has the chance to become the quickest to 1000 Test runs for New Zealand and overtake Devon Conway who achieved that feat in this inning only. 59 runs away! And... SECOND NEW BALL HAS BEEN TAKEN!

OUT! CHOPPED ON! Poor shot selection and Henry Nicholls departs. This one lands outside off on the rough and turns back in quite sharply, it keeps a shade low as well. Henry Nicholls looks to cut it buts gets a thick inside edge and the ball shatters the stumps. Henry Nicholls returns with New Zealand trailing by 166 runs.
Slightly shorter and on off, Henry Nicholls defends it to silly point.

The second new ball is available but Pakistan have decided not to take it immediately. Also, Babar Azam is back on the field and the crowd is making a lot of noise. He has a word with Nauman Ali and now the reserve umpire is seen coming onto the field. He tosses up the new ball to one of the Pakistan players who passes it on to Alex Wharf.
The length is on the shorter side, landing around off and turning back in slowly, Henry presses back and guides it through point for a single.
Quicker one, skidding in from around middle, Williamson helps it behind square leg and picks up a single.
Short and around off, Williamson goes deep inside the crease and cuts. Finds the point fielder.
Slower through the air, pitching full and around off, Williamson again defends it patiently off the front foot.
Loopy delivery, landing full on off, Williamson strides forward and defends it back.
Flighted and on middle, Henry gets back and tucks it through backward square leg for a single.
Tossed up outside leg, Kane pads it away.
FOUR! Consecutive boundaries! Again Nauman serves it outside leg, targeting the rough with a fuller-length ball, Williamson kneels and sweeps it nicely to fine leg for another boundary.

Very full and on middle, drifting in, Kane drives it back and the bowler stops it to his left.
A touch short and on off, turning in, Nicholls gets the chance to go on the back foot as he pushes it down to long on for a run.
Lands it full and outside off, Nicholls goes down and across to sweep but misses. He is hit on the back thigh and the ball deflects away towards slip.
Flighted and full around off, Kane is on the front foot as he defends it on the leg side.
Fuller around leg, Nicholls sweeps it down to fine leg for a single.
Loopy and full on off, Nicholls defends it off his front foot.
A touch short and on middle, Henry goes back and works it with the spin through square leg for a couple.

FOUR! Bang! Too full this time, around off, Henry Nicholls latches onto it and smacks it past the bowler for a cracking boundary at long off. Kane Williamson was seen taking cover as he goes down on the ground.
Googly around off, Nicholls punches it from the crease to mid on.
Tossed up around off, Williamson is watchful as he defends it off the front foot.
FOUR! Fine footwork! Nauman flights this one around middle, full in length, Kane Williamson dances down the track and lifts it cleanly over the bowler's head for a boundary.
Fuller and on middle, defended.

Was that a stumping chance? Nauman gives this one some extra flight and lands it full around off. The ball lands and turns away a bit, Kane Williamson stretches forward to drive but misses and Sarfaraz Ahmed fails to gather the ball. Kane is outside the crease as he goes off balance but survives a stumping opportunity.
Fuller and on middle, defended wristily to the leg side.
Flighted delivery, full and around off, Williamson pushes it away with an angled bat and the first slip fielder quickly moves across to his right to stop the ball with a slide.
Quicker and around leg at 86 clicks, Nicholls sticks on the back foot and defends it down.
Leans forward to a full ball and taps it down on one bounce to silly point.
Turns it with the spin to the leg side towards square leg. Another confusion over a run which is not taken.
Beats the batter in flight and length. Full and floated, around off, Nicholls fails to get forward and just defends it somehow from the crease.
A touch short and around leg, Henry Nicholls goes on the back foot and defends it to mid-wicket.
Abrar begins with a flighted delivery, full and down the leg side, Williamson sweeps it towards fine leg and picks up a single.

Momentum has not stayed for long in one corner in this Test match. It has swung back in Pakistan's favour at the moment and with a lead of 193 runs in the bag, they can call the shots in the afternoon session. How will New Zealand respond? Do join us at 1.10 pm IST (7.40 am GMT) to find out.

Neil Wagner comes up for a quick chat. He says that it's a tough pitch for the fast bowlers and it's different from what they do at home. Adds that they need to try and attack and they have not lost wickets so it's a good thing. Mentions that as the game goes on they need to keep on going and put more pressure on the opponents. Ends by saying that the short balls are harder to face as the pitch is showing some variable bounce.

Pitch report - There are a lot of footmarks on the pitch and there were a few deliveries that stayed low on Day 2. The pitch is expected to die down more and staying disciplined with the line is going to be the key for the bowlers. The surface is still a good one for batting.

In reply, the New Zealand batters, Devon Conway and Tom Latham looked solid from the beginning after coming out to bat. Even though Pakistan introduced spin pretty early in the innings, they were unable to make inroads into the Kiwi batting order. Latham is batting on 78* and Conway is on 82*. Devon Conway did get a lifeline once in the game and he will look to make the most use of it. Which side will dominate the 'moving day'? We shall find out shortly. Stay tuned...

Hello and a warm welcome to the Day 3 of the New Zealand tour of Pakistan. The hosts dominated the first day and the second day was dominated by the visitors. The opening pair of visitors remained unbeaten on 165 runs last evening. They now trail by 273 runs with all 10 wickets in the bank. The Pakistani bowlers will have to come up with something different now and bag some early wickets otherwise they could be in for a leather hunt. Which way will this Test match move? Stay with us to find out.

This Test match is hanging in the balance after a resounding batting show from the Kiwi batters. Pakistan were made to toil hard on a pitch where they didn't get much support. The only opportunity they created was against Devon Conway when he was on 57 but that appeal for caught behind was not entertained by the umpire and the hosts didn't take the DRS. Later on, the UltraEdge detected a faint edge. Apart from that moment, the New Zealand openers didn't give an iota of chance to the home side to have their say. Will the picture change on Day 3? Do join us on Wednesday at 10.30 am IST (5 am GMT) to find out. Cheers!

Never judge a pitch unless both teams have batted on it at least once, that's the usual saying! When Pakistan batted, it looked like a tough pitch due to their initial reckless approach but then the likes of Babar Azam, Sarfaraz Ahmed and Agha Salman showed that there are no demons in it. The same impression was given by the Kiwi openers who batted with authority and used all their skills to keep the Pakistan spinners at bay. Both Latham and Conway looked in command at the crease. They employed sweeps and reverse sweeps with aplomb and never allowed Abrar Ahmed and Nauman Ali to dictate terms.

Pakistan had the advantage heading into Day 2 but after losing Babar Azam in the first over of the morning session, it appeared that the Kiwis will quickly wrap up their innings. But Agha Salman stood like a rock and formed a few handy stands with the lower order. He stroked his maiden Test hundred as well and helped Pakistan reach a commanding total in the first innings.

An eventful day of Test cricket comes to a close! New Zealand have responded brilliantly with the bat and brought down the deficit to 273 runs with all 10 wickets in the kitty. The tourists will be immensely pleased with the way they performed on Day 2 and that has put them on level terms.
